newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom first-half profit jumps 18.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom first-half profit jumps 18.9 pct.

text.p: State-owned France Telecom, due to be partially privatised next year, reported on Wednesday an 18.9 percent rise in first-half profit, helped by lower debt and falling interest rate costs.

Net attributable profit for the six months to the end-June rose to 6.3 billion francs from 5.3 billion, it said in a statement. But the telecommunications operator dismissed a report in Le Monde newspaper that it had forecast a net profit for the full year of at least 10 billion francs.
The 1996 accounts would be drawn up according to U.S. GAAP accounting methods and "would not be comparable to those of 1996. All estimates for the 1996 results are thus extremely premature," it said.
The half-year results were the last drawn up according to the accounting methods used by France Telecom since 1991. France Telecom is due to be partially privatised in the spring of 1997.

Half-year profit rise was driven mainly by a fall in financing costs linked to lower debt and a reduction in interest rates. Turnover rose two percent to 75.1 billion francs from 73.6 billion. Operating profits rose 2.7 percent to 15.2 billion francs from 14.8 billion in 1995.
